__comment: OAuth 1.0a (HMAC-SHA1) replaces any username/password validator. customUI hosts the consent webview (like com.palm.eas / com.palm.skype); getAuthorizeUrl runs OAuth leg 1 (request_token) and returns the authorize URL + request token/secret, Atlas captures oauth_verifier from the redirect to Config.CALLBACK_URL, then exchangeCode runs leg 3 (access_token) and returns the stored token credentials. Flickr is a PHOTO source only - no DOCUMENTS capability, no files app.
__comment2: com.palm.app.flickr-auth MUST be in write/readPermissions: createAccount runs under the customUI auth app's identity and is permission-checked against these lists (accounts/handlers/create.js -> Utils.hasPermission). Working templates (teams/telegram/skype/dropbox) list their own auth app, not com.palm.app.accounts.
__comment3: com.palm.service.flickr is in read+writePermissions so the service itself can readCredentials(accountId) to sign photo-provider calls. Flickr OAuth 1.0a tokens do NOT expire/rotate, so writeCredentials is effectively unused after create (kept for symmetry).

capabilityProviders.__comment: Makes the Flickr account a photo source. implementation/hooks point at the stock Photos AGGREGATOR (com.palm.service.photos), which discovers PHOTO.UPLOAD accounts and (via a templateId->serviceName case in its Utils.js - added by photos-integration) calls com.palm.service.flickr/listAlbums+listPhotos, then downloads bytes with the curl-patched Sync-Manager. src_big is a live.staticflickr.com static URL (the id_secret pair is the capability; the curl -L fetch needs no auth header).
